sections.title: Introduction
sections.text:
Alterac Pass is a 3-lane Map belonging to the Warcraft universe.
The signature Objective of this Map are Cavalries. One per lane,
they will fight alongside the team who freed them from Prison Camps,
buffing allied Heroes nearby.

sections.title: Lane Assignments
sections.text:
Here you can find one or more formations
that are viable on this Map. Keep in mind that positions in lane
are not strict and will often change based on the situation.

sections.title: Formation 1-3-1
Map Strategy
sections.text:
At 0:30 minutes or whenever available, start clearing the allied Siege Camp
and capture it as soon as possible, then push with it.
Heroes who are covering the side lanes should join for the push
when there is nothing to soak in their lanes.
Ideally, you should capture this Mercenary Camp even during the Objective phase.
If you want to contest the Objective, be careful not to die in the process
otherwise your team will have fewer Heroes to push with Cavalries
and the enemy team will have an easier time defending their Structures.
The first Objective of the game is not that powerful,
so you should still prioritize soaking during it.
If you want to give the Objective, poke enemy Heroes
that are trying to capture it and do one of the following things:
capture the allied Siege Camp, capture the
Boss Camp that is on the opposite side
from the Objective, or push in the lane that
is on the opposite side from the Objective. The enemy team will be
near the Objective and thus will take longer to respond far away.
If you win the Objective, push in the side lane
that is on the same side as the Objective was because the next Objective
will be on the opposite side and, if you manage to get the Fort,
the enemy team will have to defend that lane from Reavers.
Also, if you do not clear waves immediately, you can accumulate
Minions behind Cavalries to empower your push
once they reach enemy Structures.
If you lose the Objective, try to match the amount of enemy Heroes
that are attacking each lane. If you think that you will not be able
to save a Fort or Keep, however, you should leave that lane and try
to save another Fort or Keep instead. Use single target damage
on Cavalries and area-of-effect
damage on both Minions and Cavalries at the same time.
After about 10:00 minutes, whenever your team has an advantage
while there is no Objective to contest or right after all allied Cavalries
have been killed, you can capture a Boss Camp,
then capture the other Boss Camp if available, and then push
with the last Boss you captured. Avoid doing it earlier if you do not have
a dedicated team composition.
If you are fairly confident that the enemy team is doing
a Boss Camp, start clearing the other one.
This strategy is meant to deny a double Boss Camp to the enemy team.
If it becomes too dangerous (because the enemy team
was not actually doing a Boss Camp or because you
started the other Boss Camp too late), stop doing it.

sections.title: Mercenary Camps
sections.text:
As shown in the image below, Alterac Pass has a total of 4 Mercenary Camps:
1 Boss Camp (red icon) in the top lane;
2 Siege Camps (green icon) in the middle lane;
1 Boss Camp (red icon) in the bottom lane.
Mercenary Camps on Alterac Pass disappear from the battlefield
once the Cavalries begin spawning (unless their Mercenaries are in combat)
and reappear only after all Cavalries have been killed.

Mercenary Camps indicated with a red icon are immune to Bribe effects.

sections.title: Siege Camp
sections.text:
This type of Mercenary Camp features 3 Gnolls. Once captured,
it spawns the same unit fighting for your team in the corresponding lane.
When possible, push with them to get more value.
Spawn Time
Respawn Delay
0:30 minutes
1:30 minutes after its last capture
Baseline Experience
Experience Scaling
180 Experience
+6 Experience per minute (*)
(*) For this Mercenary Camp, Experience starts scaling after 1 minute.
Gnolls have a lot of Health and can reduce the Armor
of enemy Heroes and enemy Structures, therefore they are great for
pushing with multiple Heroes.

sections.title: Boss Camp
sections.text:
This type of Mercenary Camp features 1 Ice Giant. Once captured,
it spawns the same unit fighting for your team in the corresponding lane.
When possible, push with it to get more value.
Spawn Time
Respawn Delay
5:00 minutes
5:00 minutes after its last capture
Baseline Experience
Experience Scaling
750 Experience
+10 Experience per minute (*)
(*) For this Mercenary Camp, Experience starts scaling after 1 minute.
While in combat, the Ice Giant will use Mega Smash (10-second cooldown)
to damage and Stun all enemies in melee range
and Ice Shard (15-second cooldown) to damage
and Slow enemies who get hit by them.
While being hit by Ice Shard is not lethal on its own, being
Slowed by 50% may cause you to be hit by the next Smash,
so you should always dodge Ice Shard like you do for Mega Smash.
Due to being Elite, this Mercenary Camp is immune to Bribe
effects (such as Covert Mission by Nova).

sections.title: Map Objective
sections.text:
The signature Objective of Alterac Pass consists of Cavalries locked
inside Prison Camps protected by Guards. In order to free up Cavalries,
Heroes have to distract or kill Guards, channel
for 3 seconds and then defend the area until the progress completes.
Once free, Cavalries spawn in each lane and buff nearby Heroes with
30% Movement Speed and 10% more damage.
While the timer is going, it can be paused or stopped by the enemy team.
The progress is paused while enemy Heroes are channeling.
The progress is stopped after enemy Heroes channel for 3 seconds or Guards
channel for 6 seconds without being interrupted
by crowd control or damage.
Spawn Time
Respawn Delay
3:00 minutes
from 1:50 to 2:30 minutes, reduced by 2 seconds per minute of Game Time elapsed

Prison Camps
Capture the enemy Prison Camp to summon your Cavalry. Camps can be retaken by Heroes and Minions, so guard them well!
Cavalry
Cavalry soldiers charge down each lane when summoned granting increased damage and movement speed to nearby Allied Heroes.
Generals
Each team's Core has been replaced by a General who fights against attacking enemies. Destroying a Keep reduces the General's Armor and damage.

sections.title: Prison Camps
sections.text:
Prison Camps spawn in 2 possible sets: either 2 top or 2 bottom, one per team.
Their positions will keep alternating through the course of the game,
so you will always know in which lane the next Objective will be.
The first team who frees Cavalries from Prison Camps will spawn one Cavalry per lane.
Activate the Prison Camp and then wait for the timer to ends. While active,
they spawn a Regeneration Globe for your team at 66% and 100% progress.
The timer lasts 25 seconds, plus 10 seconds for each following Objective phase, up to 55 seconds.
Guards and Heroes can deactivate the Prison Camp to stop the timer.
Heroes will also pause the timer while trying to deactivate the Prison Camp.
The first team to finish opening the Prison Camp will win the Objective.
Right before winning the Objective, you should ideally prepare waves
so that allied Cavalries reach enemy Structures at the same time in
every lane and thus the enemy team cannot easily defend them one at a time.
Similarly, right before losing the Objective, you can ruin waves
to weaken enemy Cavalries.

sections.title: Top Prison Camps
sections.text:
When the Prison Camps spawn top side, the left team can use poke
from behind impassable terrain near the middle Fort
to stall and can kite the enemy Guards around their Prison Camp.

sections.title: Bottom Prison Camps
sections.text:
When the Prison Camps spawn bottom side, the right team can use poke
from behind impassable terrain near the middle Fort
to stall and can kite the enemy Guards around their Prison Camp.

sections.title: Guards
sections.text:
Prison Camps are defended by Guards that spawn from nearby houses.
When you see a light inside an house, it means that a Guard is spawning.
The amount of Guards that can protect the Objective at the same time has a cap:
1 Guard for the first Objective, plus 1 Guard for each following Objective phase,
up to 4 Guards in total from the 4th Objective phase onwards.
If you do not reduce the number of Guards
below the current cap, new Guards will not spawn. Furthermore,
Guards do not regenerate their Health over time, so you can lower their Health
without killing them before committing and only kill them when needed
to channel the Objective. After killing Guards, new Guards will
take a couple of seconds to spawn and reach you.

sections.title: Mud Pits
sections.text:
There are 6 Mud Pits located at the borders to the middle area,
close to the side lanes. Any Hero who enters a Mud Pit will find
their Movement Speed reduced by 16% per second, to a maximum of 60%,
for as long as they remain there. Upon finding solid ground,
the Hero will regain Movement Speed at 50% per second.

sections.title: Reavers
sections.text:
Catapults on Alterac Pass are replaced by Reavers. Contrary to Catapults,
Reavers will walk in lane in front of other Minions, tanking damage for them.
This characteristic makes them extremely powerful if left unchecked
because Minions from multiple waves can build up behind them and, since
Minions deal 200% bonus damage to Structures, easily destroy them.

sections.title: Core Ability
sections.text:
Cores on Alterac Pass are replaced by Generals, who can move and fight against attacking enemies.
Generals have 20 Armor for each lane with a Fort or Keep still up. When in combat,
they will use Charge (6-second cooldown) to dash towards enemy Heroes and
Whirlwind (12-second cooldown) to deal area of effect damage.
When out of combat, they will quickly regenerate Health (about 1% per second).

sections.title: Health Regeneration
sections.text:
When trying to kill the enemy General on this Map, you have to be sure that
it will go down! Contrary to other Maps, where the enemy Core stays damaged
and only regenerates its Shield, any failed attempt to kill a General on Alterac Pass
is going to be completely nullified by their Health Regeneration. The time wasted
for trying and failing to kill a General is better used to destroy an enemy Keep,
so that you get Reavers in that lane and thus increase the pressure on the enemy team.

sections.title: Armor
sections.text:
To min-max the damage done to the enemy General while trying to end the game,
you should also consider if it is worth to destroy an already damaged Keep
in order to remove 20 Armor from the enemy General, or directly going for the General.
Generals gain 405 maximum Health per minute for 20 minutes (excluding the first minute),
up to 28100 maximum Health at 21:00 minutes. Keeps have 22550 (not scaling) maximum Health.
When trying to end the game on Alterac Pass, you should do as follows:
if there are 2 Keeps remaining and one of the Keeps is below 50% Health,
destroy that Keep and then go for the General, else go for the General directly;
if there is 1 Keep remaining and that Keep is below 30% Health,
destroy that Keep and then go for the General, else go for the General directly.
Note that having Gnolls from the Siege Camp in the middle lane changes
these thresholds because, when they hit enemies with Basic Attacks,
they reduce their Armor. In that case you should
generally take down the middle Keep regardless of its maximum Health.

sections.title: Win Conditions
sections.text:
To win the game on Alterac Pass, you should count on
any of the following win conditions:
Map Objective,
Boss Camp;
Gnolls from Siege Camp.

sections.title: Tips and Tricks
sections.text:
Use the first Healing Fountain (2-minute cooldown) before 1:00 minute
because the first Objective on this Map activates at 3:00 minutes,
so you will have it back in time for that.
Guards protecting an isolated Prison Camp (top-right or bottom-left)
can be kited around it for not taking damage.
Heroes with Summons (notably Anub'arak) or Clones
can easily solo-activate a Prison Camp without killing Guards.
Guards protecting any Prison Camp should ideally not be killed,
except when they do not let you channel
the Objective, because they cannot regenerate Health but
killing them will cause new Guards to spawn with full Health.
Given how the Objective on Alterac Pass works, you can almost win the Objective,
retreat to recover from that battle, try to stop the enemy team
from winning the Objective, and then get some kills to win the Objective
or to easily defend your Structures in case you lose the Objective.
Boss Camps are disabled while Cavalries are alive.
To play around the enemy team getting a Boss right after their Cavalries expire,
start going to a camp before the last Cavalry dies. If they are there, you could fight.
If they are not, you could take the Boss while they are taking the other one.
Global Heroes should ideally take care
of the lane that is farther away from the next Objective location,
so that they can use their global tool
to quickly join their team during the next Objective phase.
See our Map Guides page for further information »
